items.excerpt: The new Energy Materials Acceleration Platform (E-MAP) at the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT) enables a systematic examination, evaluation, and targeted refining of thousands of material variants. It links automated experiments with precise material characterization, thus creating the foundation for the accelerated development of energy materials.
items.title: Self-driving lab speeds up materials development

items.excerpt: A research team from the School of Physics at Renmin University of China has developed PhononBench, a large-scale phonon-based benchmark for evaluating the dynamical stability of AI-generated crystal materials. By combining the MatterSim-v1 universal machine-learning interatomic potential with Phonopy, the study enables high-throughput phonon-spectrum calculations for more than 130,000 AI-generated crystal structures. The benchmark systematically evaluates the dynamical stability of crystals generated by different AI models, identifies 32,995 MatterSim-labeled dynamically stable crystal structures under a strict phonon-frequency criterion, and provides a web-based platform for rapid phonon-spectrum calculation and dynamical-stability assessment.
items.title: Phononbench: A large-scale benchmark reveals the dynamical stability challenge in AI-generated crystals

items.excerpt: The novel physics-constrained AI framework PHICS realizes a full closed loop spanning multiscale inverse design and experimental validation. Leveraging interface, phase, and carrier engineering, PHICS breaks long-standing material trade-offs to yield composite phase-change materials that achieve simultaneous enhancements in thermal conductivity and electrical insulation while maintaining high thermal storage density, paving new pathways for designing advanced electronic thermal management materials.
items.title: Physics-constrained machine learning for the inverse design of multifunctional composites

items.excerpt: A new way of measuring how materials interact at the atomic level could help scientists develop better-performing, longer-lasting batteries.
items.title: X-ray method predicts anion behavior, opening path to longer-lasting batteries and AI-assisted chemistry

items.excerpt: Tiny insects called aphids inject hundreds of mysterious proteins into plants, hijacking the plants' own genomes to build galls: structures made of plant tissue but constructed to the insects' specifications to house and feed their offspring.
items.title: Shared blueprint in aphid proteins helps AI predict their structures

items.excerpt: Publishing original research in a top-tier academic journal has been an ambition of Arsalaan Ahmad's since he enrolled in an undergraduate computer science program at Cardiff University.
items.title: By cutting data layers, researchers create fast, explainable landslide detection AI

items.excerpt: University of Missouri researchers are using artificial intelligence to uncover hidden clues among the trillions of bacteria living in the human gut, including changes that could one day help scientists detect diseases earlier. The Mizzou team—which brings together expertise in medicine, data science and engineering—developed a new machine-learning tool capable of finding biological signals that conventional methods miss. Their paper is published in the journal mSystems.
items.title: AI tool finds biological signals in the gut microbiome that other methods miss, may flag early signs of disease

items.excerpt: A research team at InfoLab, Sungkyunkwan University (SKKU), led by Professor Tamer Abuhmed, has developed a new vision transformer architecture called the 4D fMRI CrossFormer (4DfCF) to analyze four-dimensional functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data.
items.title: New method makes AI brain-disorder screening more transparent and computationally efficient

items.excerpt: Artificial intelligence (AI) models prioritize starkly different attributes than humans when making high-stakes decisions, and they don't express indecision like humans do, according to a new study led by Penn State researchers. The findings raise questions about the role of AI in decision support for ethically sensitive situations like medical decisions.
items.title: Who gets the kidney? AI chatbots do not make the same moral choices humans do

items.excerpt: With the rapid rise of artificial intelligence in daily life, software coding has become increasingly automated, with powerful AI systems known as coding agents able to write and revise computer programs almost autonomously. But what happens when an AI agent must contend not just with digital command lines, but with the physical world of robotics?
items.title: Open-source benchmark tests whether AI agents can engineer working robots

items.excerpt: Artificial intelligence models can give users the wrong answer and do so with great confidence. They can also hedge and warn that they are unsure—even when they get the answer right.
items.title: Making AI more trustworthy by making it red-flag its own doubtful answers

items.excerpt: QC Design reports that its Meridian AI system achieved over 10x lower logical error rates than published methods across 100+ quantum design tasks.
items.title: QC Design Reports 10x Logical Error Reduction With Meridian AI

items.excerpt: Richard de Grijs looks at how the Roman Space Telescope will change astronomy forever
items.title: How the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will turn the sky into a dataset – Physics World

items.excerpt: Imagine a neighbor who persistently claims you make noise at night. Others initially disagree, but the neighbor keeps trying to convince them. Their success depends not only on their stubbornness but also on how well connected they are and how willing others are to change their minds.
items.title: When stubbornness becomes a security problem: How AI agents can manipulate others

items.excerpt: A new wave of radiology practices are aggressively embracing AI: developing and deploying it in-house, and marketing themselves as 'AI-native.'
items.title: In radiology, AI is blurring the line between technology development and clinical practice

items.excerpt: Researchers discover an association between affective generative AI use and mental health problems in youth.
items.title: AI Use and Emotional Problems in Children and Teens
